newsitem.title: USA: Brazil's Copel files offering with US SEC.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Copel files offering with US SEC.

text.p: Brazilian electrical power firm Companhia Paranaense de Energia (Copel) filed Monday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to register an offering of American depositary shares representing an undetermined amount of Class B preferred shares.
Underwriters for the offering are Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Lehman Brothers, according to the SEC filing.
The company said it expects to raise about $393 million, or $452 million if the underwriters' over-allotment option is exercised, from the U.S. offering and a concurrent overseas offering.

About $80 million of the proceeds will be used for capital expenditures related to the company's Salto Caxias hydroelectic facility. In addition, $230 million will be used to expand and upgrade transmission and distribution systems. The remainder will be used to retire outstanding debt maturing in August 1997.

As of April 25, the State government directly owned 60 percent of the company's common shares and indirectly it owned an additional 26 percent. Under Brazilian law, the government must own at least 60 percent of the company's common shares.
